Subject: RE: Recent private cluster upgrade - control plane instability (internal triage)

Jonas / Naomi — quick summary from initial triage:
- We saw a backlog of control-plane handshakes tied to a credentials refresh loop on the management agent. The agent's retry backoff was not being applied because the new agent binary included a signal-handling change that bypassed the jitter window.
- That caused a burst of near-simultaneous handshake attempts which overwhelmed the controlplane connection accept queue for a subset of nodes.
- The change is in component tag: rwi-agent v2.7.1 -> v2.8.0 (rolled last night). We reproduce locally with the same binary and a simulated high-connection churn.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Hotfix: revert agent to v2.7.1 on affected nodes (fast, safe)
2) Config: temporarily increase accept queue and add explicit jitter in agent config (medium effort)
3) Full rollback of the release (heavier, more risk)

Recommend option 1 for the bridge to stop the backlog and option 2 as a follow-up to prevent recurrence. I'll prepare a small runbook for the rollback that runs node-by-node to avoid mass reconnects. Attaching a brief timeline spreadsheet.

Ben
VP, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary: agent handshake backlog during v2.8.0 rollout

Lena / Tom / Acme Ops team —

Thanks again for working with us on the bridge last week. This thread is the final post-incident summary and the artifacts we promised.

What happened: after the v2.8.0 agent rollout, a change to signal handling removed a small randomized jitter from the credentials refresh loop. That caused many agents to attempt handshakes at near-identical intervals, which saturated the connection accept queue on a subset of management nodes.

Impact: several onboarding API calls timed out for ~30–45 minutes for a portion of traffic. Model deployment jobs for a small set of tenants experienced retries and delayed starts. No customer data was exposed or corrupted.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Staggered rollback to agent v2.7.1 on affected nodes between 09:05–09:22 PT (option 1). Handshake rates returned to normal within 8 minutes of the first rollback.
- Temporary increase to accept queue settings for the subset of controlplane nodes as a safety buffer.
- We collected full traces and correlated timestamps with your provided controlplane-trace.txt (thanks).

Preventive actions and follow-ups:
- Reintroduce deterministic jitter to the credentials refresh path and add an integration test to simulate high churn (target ship: v2.8.1).
- Add automated canary that monitors accept-queue saturation and halts rollout if thresholds are exceeded.
- We will run a joint upgrade rehearsal with Acme on a staging cluster next month.

- rootcause-postmortem.pdf (attached)
